newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha slides for fourth day running.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha slides for fourth day running.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices lost ground on Thursday for the fourth successive trading day in reaction to slightly weaker overnight crudes in London, traders said.

Bids for first-half January open-spec naphtha were heard at $211.00, with offers at about $213.00. It was bought by a Japanese trading house at $212.75 on Wednesday. The seller is believed to be a western trader.
Second-half January was assessed at $210.50/$212.00, down from late Wednesday's $211.50/$212.00.
Naphtha prices fell about $8.00 over the last week against a backdrop of sliding crude prices.
In inter-month naphtha spreads, first-half January versus first-half February was quoted unchanged from Wednesday at plus $1.50/$2.50.
In the middle distillates market, kerosene traders were relaxed with requirements by early December having been satisfied.

Levels for mid and late December cargoes were notionally quoted at plus $1.50 to $1.80 over the mean of Singapore quotes on a cost and freight (C and F) basis. The levels were widely discussed due to scarcity of recent deals, traders said.
